title: Strutting Out of the Woodwork: The “New” Racism, the Rise of the Trumpian Albocracy and its Collaborators
author: John G. Russell
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/04/IMG_3645-680x510.jpg)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

> “Calling us racist doesn’t work anymore.”
>
> – [Brandon Gill](https://www.thedailybeast.com/maga-rep-brandon-gills-post-
> about-leftwing-criticism-of-racism-immediately-backfires/)
>
> “Let them call you racist. Let them call you xenophobes. Let them call you
> nativist. Wear it as a badge of honor.”
>
> – [Steve Bannon](https://www.facebook.com/Channel4News/videos/steve-bannon-
> addresses-the-national-front-in-france/10155762537696939/)
>
> “Sometimes Minnesotans are so afraid that you’re going to call us a racist,
> you’re going to call us an Islamophobe, you’re going to call us some name
> that we just don’t want to get into that fight. You know what, I would argue
> that I never did care, but I’m done being careful, even the least bit
> careful.”
>
> – [Tom Emmer](https://www.facebook.com/CSPAN/videos/rep-tom-emmer-r-mn-the-
> third-ranking-house-republican-said-somali-immigrants-sho/886239441184458/)

They no longer hide in the woodwork. In Donald Trump’s America, racism has
become a badge of honor, worn with pride by the icy posses of the right, his
deputized agents of hate, and other self-proclaimed “patriots.”

Those who decry the rise of the “new antisemitism” remain silent on the old
racism, which isn’t old at all, merely less flamboyantly expressed. Today,
this new variation boldly emerges from the shadows of what was once called
“polite racism,” “[banal racism](https://law.stanford.edu/2019/10/16/the-
banality-of-bigotry/),” or what Jared Taylor, the founder of the white
nationalist  _American Renaissance,_ euphemistically touts as “[race
realism](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/aug/26/jared-taylor-alt-
right-clinton-trump).” Whatever you call it, under Trump, the right’s “Hope
and Change” mirror-universe Obama, racism has been normalized, as an expanding
swath of white America, seeking scapegoats for the nation’s moral and economic
decline, anxiously frets about the rising tide of color they fear will replace
them and “their values.” The fact that among these fretters are individuals
from the very groups comprising that tide, such as [Black Voices for Trump,
](https://www.facebook.com/BlackVoicesforTrump20/) [Latinos for
Trump,](https://www.facebook.com/LatinosForTrump/) and [Indian Americans for
Trump](https://www.facebook.com/indiansfortrump/) – should give pause, if only
to recognize that racism, like other oppressive, classify-and-conquer systems,
requires collaborators.

Megyn Kelly, the former Fox News and NBC News host turned meltdown podcaster,
who once insisted that Jesus and Santa Claus are white, defended blackface,
and [raged against the New Black
Panthers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iHIYoMMuUzs) [1], only to issue
disingenuous [apologies](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EDni4xqxlBQ) when her
racism was called out, now angrily demands that Haitians [“go back to fucking
Haiti.”](https://www.facebook.com/TheHaitianAmerican/videos/conservative-
commentator-megyn-kelly-unleashed-a-fiery-profanity-filled-rant-
on-/1575763197502540/) She accuses them of being unassimilable because they
have not adopted the work ethic of a country built in large part on the backs
of enslaved blacks[2] as their owners exalted the virtues of liberty,
equality, and the rights of white men. Although she faced another social media
backlash, this time Kelly has not apologized. Immersed in the blooming
rejecting pool of toxic hate that is social media, she has turned vociferous
race-baiting into her brand, her disdain for black and brown people fueling
her podcasting fame and profitability.

Not to be outdone, Trump has
[proclaimed](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=9d11f09b99ad9e2b&rlz=1C5CHFA_enJP899JP899&udm=39&fbs=ABfTbFVyMZGZf1hfvX9uKjN_-G8cY2oODYyTyZk24Xz37_7FQ0Kuh3jfnRqiKzI7KrGsO-
ahMiVxElJGh2HXmqeqNBF0cQXdmpTgObSkiMYY2Gkv4zU_pOqRXxdXxnfdJF0FHo7yiPijvNwsua6Mi1Zg6OmgJFpHDhsW7yJ4LNCSUVM2vawakG0dhnQIqRaVGrl0bUUT1KuGGHS_6Zy094dtewvXAT0DZA&q=trump+calls+somalians+garbage&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiEqMf0hK-
VAxXAXOsIHfNuMUsQs6gLegQIEhAB&biw=1276&bih=1131&dpr=1.33#fpstate=ive&ip=1&vld=cid:4704fbf3,vid:9l_qFbrXdss,st:0)
that he does not want Somalis “in our country,” labeling them “garbage.”[3]A
year ago, Trump’s supporters would have deflected by telling us that the
president was simply being his usual straight-talking self or joking, though
this “joke” seemed to be cribbed from comedian Tony Hinchcliffe, another
unapologetic [trash
talker](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=f2286370e303522b&rlz=1C5CHFA_enJP899JP899&sxsrf=APpeQnscjvZSeXKrpdmjMIPWz6bC-
btV1g:1785319749213&udm=39&fbs=ABfTbFVyMZGZf1hfvX9uKjN_-G8cxpBkeIeqYwoCbfNVc4vKE7plZzta63Pe5DpJ3XFR9Xy5hkFmhg6pfO_X-
sED2CqEDfLQbWLcDMRztF_yUReEECN6eR27h7XUG7HTKs0ZMau9pzZ8PWvEAZ1RZhElPC707SSNa5IZK4CsuDh2AcdDUBquFGfuiQR6r-b9uQUixL11913Zv_QBThcIwA8L5r_r7jI5Jw&q=tony+Hinchcliffe+garbage&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjvgNmr0veVAxX2s1YBHc9TPWoQs6gLegQIFhAB&biw=1984&bih=1081&dpr=1.33#fpstate=ive&ip=1&vld=cid:ea94d227,vid:bBXiXqRlQMY,st:0).
Today, they double down. Seven years ago, Trump
[denied](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-denies-he-used-profane-
language-to-describe-african-countries) he called Haiti and African nations
“shithole countries.” Now, he
[confirms](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/12/10/politics/video/trump-confirms-
he-think-african-countries-are-shitholes-digvid-vrtc) he did. He has
repeatedly told Rep. Ilhan Omar to “go back to your country,” the latest
instance occurring at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner,
where – this time uninterrupted – he performed his signature vile rally
material.

Trump is not alone. Representative Tom Emmer[
tells](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/91ynulc7cvY) a predominantly white Faith
and Freedom Coalition audience in Washington, D.C. that if visitors to America
“don’t assimilate, then they should go the hell back to wherever they came
from,” a remark welcomed with enthusiastic applause. While his immediate
target is Minnesota’s Somali community, his use of “wherever” left the
geographic boundary conveniently vague. His phraseology makes clear that he
meant people – to borrow the president’s slur – from “shithole countries.”
However, despite his self-professed “aggressive-aggressive” temperament, he
fails to tell the Somalis this to their faces.

Immigrants and refugees of color stand accused of rejecting Christian American
values. In keeping with the conference, Emmer presents himself as a defender
of those values, though judging by his statements, he seems unfamiliar with
Luke 10:30-37 and Luke 17:11-19, biblical passages in which despised
Samaritans prove more compassionate than their detractors. More disturbingly,
and contrary to Luke’s teachings, Emmer’s remarks suggest he believes his
faith allows him to reject modern-day Samaritans, regardless of their actions,
simply because they are Samaritans.

Ironically, the targets of the diversity-averse right are remarkably diverse,
unified only by the threat their pigmentation and alleged inability to
assimilate pose to the ablocracy. Alongside  _de rigueur_ anti-black and brown
rhetoric, when it comes to anti-Indian American racism, MAGA’s marching morons
are legion.

Brandon Gill has called Indian Americans “7-Eleven workers,” which means he
can take advantage of its family benefit program because his wife, Danielle
D’Souza, is the daughter of Dinesh D’Souza, the felonious conservative Indian
American political pundit. Gill has also circulated [ a
petition](https://www.newsweek.com/petition-deport-ilhan-omar-brandon-
gill-2030520) calling for the deportation of his House colleague Omar and told
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani to “[go back to the Third
World](https://midmichigannow.com/news/nation-world/house-republicans-condemn-
mamdani-for-eating-with-bare-hands-go-back-to-the-third-world).” He has
accused those who confront racism as themselves being racist, taking to heart
General Todd Blanche’s [accusation](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/federal-
grand-jury-charges-southern-poverty-law-center-wire-fraud-false-statements-
and) that the Southern Poverty Law Center is “manufacturing racism to justify
its existence,” as if there were not enough of the real thing.

During the 2024 presidential election, Ann Coulter [declared
](https://www.google.com/search?sa=X&sca_esv=b1924c149c9d7e58&rlz=1C5CHFA_enJP899JP899&aep=10&cs=0&sxsrf=APpeQntFYG0zpiXcNYS-
UCVHD7TdQ_KtZw:1785201089896&udm=39&fbs=ABfTbFVyMZGZf1hfvX9uKjN_-G8cY2oODYyTyZk24Xz37_7FQ0Kuh3jfnRqiKzI7KrGsO-
ahMiVxElJGh2HXmqeqNBF0lYh5s_yQhnNY-BGVjVxwHBHAHBF2jXSGjKQAb8wOJY-
wIvpbB2IQbl7dxNenSTLRcmJ2d253fCulozS-
wa0V4l_LaCi4jmbTDkjVGzSjDmUPjmwvVA6Jp2DKHV_ZUocBY-S-
fQ&q=Ann+coulter+on+ramaswamy&ved=2ahUKEwj9gcOmmPSVAxXcdvUHHQ1WJ6wQs6gLegQIDhAB&biw=1869&bih=978&dpr=1.33#fpstate=ive&vld=cid:a83002c0,vid:4SQyWQIE2yU,st:0)she
was a “fan” of Vivek Ramaswamy, describing him as “bright” and “articulate,”
smugly clarifying that it was acceptable to label him the latter because “he’s
not an American black.” She added that while she agreed with him on “many,
many of the things he said,” she could not vote for him “because you’re an
Indian.” [4]

For its part, during the Republican primaries, Trump’s campaign [directed its
own vitriol at Nikki
Haley](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/01/19/trump-haley-race/).
Now, the [righteously
racist](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/07/18/rnc-convention-
usha-vance-maga-attacks/) vent their opprobrium at Usha Vance. All of this
proves that their acceptance of Indian Americans, like that of other Americans
of color, runs only skin-deep.

Although months in coming, to his credit, Vance did fire back at those who
attacked his wife, though defending one’s family is usually regarded as a
basic human reaction, unless, that is, you belong to the same party as Senator
[Bernie
Moreno](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/global-
trends/bernie-moreno-breaks-silence-says-max-miller-is-a-danger-to-his-
daughter/articleshow/132812816.cms?from=mdr). However, Vance has been far less
emphatic about racism directed at those outside his family, at one point even
[serving as an apologist](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/oct/15/jd-
vance-racist-messages-young-republicans-chat-leak) for the Young Republican
National Federation after hundreds of racist texts were leaked to the media.
Worse still, when DOGE staffer Marko Elez [resigned
](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/vance-says-doge-staffer-who-resigned-
after-a-report-of-racist-postings-should-be-brought-back)over his own racist
social media posts, including one in which he wrote “I was racist before it
was cool” and another that read “[Normalize Indian
hate](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c93q625y04wo),” he was [rehired thanks
to Vance](https://www.politico.com/news/2025/03/29/doge-marco-elez-software-
engineer-us-payroll-00259303), proving exactly how “cool” racism has become,
especially in the forgiving eyes of the Vice President as long as it is not
directed at his own family. Just [young’un being edgy
young’uns,](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/jd-vance/vance-young-republicans-
racism-lives-ruined-rcna237838) as the bestselling, erstwhile elegiac
hillbilly might put it. But then, what did you expect? Remember, this is the
same man who once called Trump “America’s Hitler,” only to retract it when it
served his political aspirations, and who today
[professes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jzgefEcooY0) to be against racism
and antisemitism, yet [deleted](https://newrepublic.com/post/186073/jd-vance-
scrub-blog-post-republicans-anti-immigrant-racism) his old blog posts critical
of Republican racism.

These advocates of racial chauvinism embody a bizarre paradox; they openly
express their distaste for people of color, unless they are their spouses,
children, political allies, or proverbially some of their “best friends.”
Significantly, Indian Americans have increasingly come to serve as both a
[target of their racism](https://www.wired.com/story/maga-indians-went-all-in-
on-trump/)  _and_ a convenient symbol of their “tolerance,” proving once again
that racism is as unoriginal in its rhetoric as it is paradoxically
egalitarian in its capacity for hatred.

Such racism, however, is not confined to words; it is embedded in both
domestic and foreign policy, where it takes the form of deportations, punitive
tariffs foreign aid cuts to the developing world, and unwavering support the
Israeli genocide in Gaza. The Trump regime has ended Temporary Protected
Status (TPS) for Haiti, [stripping legal
protection](https://www.npr.org/2026/07/23/nx-s1-5884947/haitians-protected-
status-tps)s from some 350,000 Haitians, a move that will trigger mass
deportations and widespread family separations. This is in addition to those
from nations in the Global South whose protections have [already expired or
been terminated.](https://www.justice.gov/eoir/temporary-protected-
status)Furthermore, TPS protections for Somali, Ethiopian, and South Sudan
nationals are in the crosshairs, currently stayed only by temporary federal
court orders, orders that Trump and his apparatchiks routinely ignore.

Institutions that once defined and enlivened American ideals are under
assault. Agencies charged with advancing America’s deferred ideals are
defunded or, like the Smithsonian Institution, labeled “[anti-
white](https://abcnews.com/Politics/scathing-report-white-house-accuses-
smithsonian-presenting-radical/story?id=134515705)” and
[disclaimed](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/07/25/world/politics/trump-
disclaimer-smithsonian/). Meanwhile, those who have promoted these ideals or
benefited from their efforts are denied promotions or fired outright under the
pretext that they are unqualified for their positions. All the while the
president and his cabinet of cronies deem themselves eminently qualified for
theirs, despite ample evidence to the contrary. One is tempted to invoke the
Peter Principle, but that concept applies to competent people who are
gradually promoted until they reach a level of incompetence; here, however,
the leadership is incompetent from the outset, insulated from failure by its
whiteness and proximity to power.

Those who have assimilated still face hostility. If your name is Obama,
Mamdani, or El-Sayed, it proves that the new racism isn’t so new after all,
only more vociferous and xenophobic, even when you are a citizen – by birth or
naturalization. Indeed, simply having an Arabic-sounding name is enough to get
you [booed](https://okcfox.com/news/nation-world/booing-of-fallen-las-vegas-
officers-name-at-trump-rally-sparks-debate), even if you are a fallen police
officer, accused of [incest](https://mace.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-
nancy-mace-moves-subpoena-ilhan-omar-and-alleged-brotherhusband-minnesota), or
labeled a [terrorist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HaDz6fDZvxo) or a
[communist](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/absolutely-communist-mamdani-
dodges-label-his-record-expert-say-otherwise). Ilhan Omar, in particular, has
become a magnet for right-wing-fueled, spurious
[rumors,](https://www.snopes.com/news/2025/12/02/ilhan-omar-brother-
marriage/?collection=471926) some of which are [spewed by
Trump](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ytl5R6IZh_Q) himself, including the
smear that she married her brother. At one point, Trump, deploying his usual
disclaimer, said he “[knows nothing about
it,](https://www.c-span.org/clip/white-house-event/president-trump-weighs-in-
on-allegation-rep-omar-was-married-to-her-brother/4808113)” although recently
he appears to have become [more
“informed”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8wd3evd_XY4) – even if that
information, like his knowledge of [Somali
society](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ytl5R6IZh_Q), is patently false and
betrays the abysmal depths of his ignorance.

This escalation of racist rhetoric has largely been met by Republicans with
indifference, when not encouraged outright, including from MAGA and,
disturbingly, the party’s own “rainbow coalition” of black-, brown- and
yellow-faced collaborators. Indeed, the only time the party seems to
appreciate diversity is when minorities from the groups it despises advance
its white nationalist, Christian nationalist, and Zionist agendas, or remain
silent about its bigotry.

Such taciturnity has plagued the GOP before – and even been criticized by its
own members. In 2019, seventeen months after the Charlottesville “Unite the
Right” march in Virginia, [Senator Tim Scott, voicing his
](https://www.scott.senate.gov/newsroom/news-coverage/tim-scott-why-are-
republicans-accused-of-racism-because-were-silent-on-things-like-this/)concern
over a rash of anti-black physical attacks, the vocal advocacy of white
supremacy by then-Rep. Steve King, and the lack of response to them by members
of his party, lamented:

"Some in our party wonder why Republicans are constantly accused of racism –
it is because of our silence when things like this are said. Immigration is
the perfect example, in which somehow our  _affection for the rule of law_ has
become conflated with a perceived racism against brown and black people.

"I do support border security not because I want to keep certain ethnicities
out of our nation, but because I support enforcing our laws. I do not care if
you come from Canada, France or Honduras;_if you break our laws, there should
be consequences_. But it has become almost impossible to have a reasonable
conversation along those lines. That’s in part why I laid out my agenda on
civility, fairness and opportunity on Thursday on the floor of the Senate
(emphasis added)."

Yet, Scott himself has since failed to find his voice to call out Trump’s
overt racism. Instead, during the 2024 presidential campaign, he[ professed to
love](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=216fa5c4d45a54f4&rlz=1C5CHFA_enJP899JP899&sxsrf=APpeQnvbpneWFd-
EBz0DwKKEFkF3Nv6hIw:1785481234401&udm=39&fbs=ABfTbFVyMZGZf1hfvX9uKjN_-G8cqu7ocb7U6ah0xpkIrGMK4JAeCmZp4riIcplhAkpcBx-8F5cZONBpzmX08C4FXBN
--
H0jScdCRYxK1M7RqQqlPqRocMp4nFC_ptsVrid0ZwC7koOrCXyEviFAqT54HCg0CiEYY6REays5oSTE5_nHs7AK_TahfFjnunvmRh0OUCaNtgZJU1Grv8BIlOix7PcmGeedTw&q=tim+scott+i+love+trump&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjN0-r1q_yVAxU5dPUHHQZ7MIcQs6gLegQIEhAB&biw=2071&bih=1123&dpr=1.33#fpstate=ive&ip=1&vld=cid:0eb31650,vid:ingY7ethJOI,st:0)
him, endorsing Trump as a president who [“doesn’t see black or
white.”](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=d9dbe7c587d79551&rlz=1C5CHFA_enJP899JP899&udm=39&fbs=ABfTbFVyMZGZf1hfvX9uKjN_-G8cqu7ocb7U6ah0xpkIrGMK4JAeCmZp4riIcplhAkpcBx-8F5cZONBpzmX08C4FXBN
--
H0jScdCRYxK1M7RqQqlPqRocMp4nFC_ptsVrid0ZwC7koOrCXyEviFAqT54HCg0CiEYY6REays5oSTE5_nHs7AK_TahfFjnunvmRh0OUCaNtgZJU1Grv8BIlOix7PcmGeedTw&q=tim+scott+i+love+trump&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjQkMDo8a2VAxW0XesIHbaHE4EQs6gLegQIFBAB&biw=1276&bih=1131&dpr=1.33#fpstate=ive&ip=1&vld=cid:52b8ab15,vid:xxQicpSQh9s,st:0)
To be fair, Scott did voice his objection to Trump’s reposting to Truth Social
of a meme that depicted the Obamas as apes,
[saying](https://www.wjcl.com/article/south-carolina-tim-scott-trump-
obamas/70270042) he was “praying it was fake because it’s the most racist
thing I’ve seen out of this White House.” Still, he needn’t have solicited
divine intervention to determine the image’s lack of authenticity, since the
Obamas are clearly not apes, though the
[right](https://www.ocregister.com/2011/04/17/oc-republican-linked-to-
offensive-obama-ape-email/) apparently [hasn’t gotten the
memo.](https://www.ocregister.com/2011/04/17/oc-republican-linked-to-
offensive-obama-ape-email/) And if Scott thinks that the meme was the most
racist thing to come out of the White House, he must be spending most of his
time in the same rehab wing Mitch McConnell occupies, or be equally brain-
dead.

One wonders if Scott is equally passionate about ensuring that those
lawbreakers face consequences even when they occupy the Oval Office and other
positions of power. Despite his earlier reprimand of his party, he has held
his tongue. Even in these inflationary times, it seems the price of
[handkerchiefs
](https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=handkerchief+head)is still
relatively cheap. Apparently, they are being discounted and sold right next to
red caps and white hoods.

If you are white, rich, and racist – move over James Weldon Johnson; we seem
to have found the new national anthem of the right – an “affection for the
rule of law” has never been the standard to which your conduct is held. This
is certainly the case today, when members of the albocracy are free to grift
[no-bid federal contracts](https://time.com/article/2026/07/06/lincoln-
memorial-reflecting-pool-repairs-Doug-Burgum-Algae-Gash/) and to have their
brainchild AI [generate sexualized images of
children](https://counterhate.com/research/grok-floods-x-with-sexualized-
images/). Meanwhile, as immigrants are demonized, scapegoated, deported, and
killed for allegedly failing to assimilate American values, homegrown
America’s homegrown “patriots” are allowed to violate those values with
impunity – escaping liability even when found guilty, like the pardoned, red-
blooded insurrectionists who, unlike Trump’s imagined Reflecting Pool vandals,
actually vandalized the Capitol, attacked police, and defecated in its halls.
A literal right-wing shitshow, though corporate media spared us the sight of
such smears.

We live in a time when trying to get America to fulfill its ideals is
considered traitorous; when to acknowledge that America has failed to realize
those ideals, even as generations have strived to attain them, and to teach
about and celebrate those who fought and died to hold the nation to its
promises, is branded un-American, a betrayal of white identity by those who
disingenuously cast themselves as the foes of identity politics.

Instead, that historical record – inspiring to some, threatening to others –
is systematically erased. Institutions that teach it are defunded, memorials
commemorating it, removed; and online government archives, redacted with a
fervor that rivals the redactions of the Epstein files. This erasure serves a
singular purpose: to obscure unpleasant facts behind a nationalist fiction
that replaces truth with hagiography and shields the guilty from justice. By
these actions, our government not only protects pedophiles; it promotes and
[beatifies](https://www.faithandfreedom.com/the-blood-of-the-martyrs-charlie-
kirks-witness-and-movement/) racists as well.

Unfortunately, some progressives view the overhyped “MAGA civil war” as a
blueprint for a “Unite the Right and the Left” coalition to defeat Trumpism,
as if these newly “woke” social injustice warriors will prove to be reliable
allies. They naively ignore an elemental truth: anti-Trumpism is not anti-
racism. Nick Fuentes, Megyn Kelly, Marjorie Taylor Greene, Alex Jones, and
Tucker Carlson may have grown disaffected with Trump and MAGA, but they remain
worshipers at the altar of white supremacy, and, in the case of [Candace
Owens](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2024/apr/02/black-radio-
conversations-with-candace-owens), YouTube’s very own [Clayton
Bigsby](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PulfeZMIAso), self-hating anti-
blackness. And while Carlson may have cut ties with Trump over the Epstein
files and the Iran War, there is no evidence he has abandoned his self-
professed discomfort with black pilots. That they have begun to question Trump
on a number of issues does not mean they are people who can be reasoned with
on the matter of race and racism; it means only that they will likely invest
their hatreds in a new messiah, who may[ ](https://time.com/7336273/marjorie-
taylor-greene-2028/)[arise from their own
ranks](https://www.mediaite.com/politics/tucker-carlson-releases-10-point-
